projects.name: Atlas Ops
projects.impact: 31% faster completion for high-frequency operational tasks
projects.problem: Users moved across several tools and dense tables to complete one task, creating missed exceptions and slow handoffs.
projects.method: Reframed the product around task states, progressive disclosure and a shared detail workspace with contextual actions.
projects.result: Usability testing showed 31% faster task completion and materially fewer navigation errors.

evidence.baseline: Before redesign, the benchmark workflow required repeated tool switching, dense table scanning and multiple context changes.
evidence.measure: Task-completion benchmark comparing the existing workflow with the redesigned task-state prototype.
evidence.confidence: Validated through moderated usability sessions using the same high-frequency operational scenario.

projects.name: Signal AI Assistant
projects.impact: Reduced analyst triage steps from 7 to 3
projects.problem: AI suggestions were difficult to trust because users could not see supporting evidence or understand downstream actions.
projects.method: Added evidence-first explanations, confidence framing, safe fallback states and reversible actions.
projects.result: The revised flow reduced triage steps and improved confidence ratings in internal usability sessions.

evidence.baseline: The original analyst path required 7 decision and navigation steps before a suggestion could be safely acted on.
evidence.measure: Step-count comparison across the same triage scenario, supported by qualitative confidence feedback.
evidence.confidence: Observed in internal usability sessions with reversible-action and evidence states enabled.

projects.name: Northstar Design System
projects.problem: Fast product growth created inconsistent patterns, duplicated components and visual drift between design and code.
projects.method: Introduced semantic tokens, component contracts, accessibility rules, QA checks and release notes shared with engineering.
projects.result: Component adoption reached 85%, while design review cycles became shorter and more predictable.

evidence.baseline: Teams maintained duplicated components and inconsistent visual rules across active product surfaces before shared governance was introduced.
evidence.measure: Adoption tracking across active surfaces plus design-to-development clarification trends during rollout.
evidence.confidence: Measured against component usage and repeated review patterns rather than self-reported maturity scores.

artifacts.label: Semantic token and component contract map

projects.name: Pulse Executive Dashboard
projects.impact: Unified 5 reporting views into one decision dashboard
projects.problem: Leaders received multiple reports with duplicated metrics and no consistent way to identify what required attention.
projects.method: Reorganized information around business questions, thresholds, alerts and progressive drill-down.
projects.result: Five recurring report views were consolidated into one responsive workspace with clearer escalation paths.

evidence.baseline: Decision-makers previously moved between 5 recurring reporting views with duplicated metrics and inconsistent escalation cues.
evidence.measure: Information-architecture inventory comparing duplicated views, decision questions and escalation paths before and after consolidation.
evidence.confidence: Verified against the recurring report set and the consolidated dashboard information model.
